title: OSPF on Junos: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Dynamic routing means routers learn paths without you typing them. O S P F is one of the best known. Let's see how Junos does it.

lines.t: Routers that learn on their own
O S P F does that

scenes.heading: The sorting hub
scenes.narration: Imagine a regional post office hub manager. They don't drive every van, but they know the map of how mail flows between hubs. The manager knows every hub in the region. Hubs must agree on the basics to cooperate. The faster the road, the cheaper the trip.

items.real: Routers in an area share one map
Same area, subnet and hello timers

scenes.heading: Turning it on
scenes.narration: The command is short. Put an interface into an area. Then check the neighbour state, and look at the routes you learned. Put the interface into an area. Check the neighbour, and look for Full. Then see what routes you learned.

lines.t: set protocols ospf area 0 interface ge-0/0/0.0

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Here are three mix-ups. O S P F still needs an I P address on the interface. It only learns routes advertised by other O S P F routers. And cost comes from bandwidth, not hops.

items.wrong: OSPF replaces the need for an IP address
items.right: It needs a valid IP on the interface

items.wrong: OSPF learns every route in the world
items.right: Only routes advertised in its area

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos OSPF lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Add each interface to an area under protocols O S P F. Neighbours must match on area, subnet and timers. Check for the Full state with show O S P F neighbor. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos OSPF lab.

points.t: set protocols ospf area N interface X
Neighbours must match: area, subnet, timers
show ospf neighbor: look for Full
